值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析法國高福利社會背後的動盪真相，打破抗議純粹源於爭取公平權益的表面迷思。
  • 揭示歐洲歷經半個世紀政治軟弱所累積的深層代價，涵蓋移民失控、執法威信瓦解與社會撕裂等核心痛點。
  • 針砭左右兩派政客為了選票而妥協的虛偽面目，直言多元文化整合政策徹底破產後的殘酷現實。

摘要

高福利神話與失控的街頭掠奪

作者描述法國街頭再度上演打砸搶燒的鬧劇，示威者表面上聲稱為了教育與未來而抗爭，實際掠奪時卻特意避開豬肉、火腿與紙張，專挑名牌精品與電子產品下手。作者指出，法國政府早已提供極其優渥的全面福利，涵蓋免費醫療、育兒津貼、免費避孕用品、漫長年假與高額租屋補助，然而過度的縱容並未換來社會安寧，反而滋養出永不滿足的索取心態與暴力藉口。

五十年政治懦弱積累的歷史帳單

作者引述一名法國民眾的見解，強調這場動盪絕非突發事件，而是法國歷經五十年左右兩派政客輪番執政、彼此妥協與退讓的制度性惡果。長年以來，當局在面對暴力與毒品犯罪時，往往以空洞的社會學說辭替罪犯開脫，建立起極度寬省與放任的文化，讓違法者習慣免除責任。作者認為整座西歐都在共同償還三大沉重債務：失敗的移民整合、難以承受的高福利開支以及選民對建制派政客信任的徹底幻滅。

法外之地的蔓延與破產的政治承諾

作者進一步指出，法國境內已有超過一千五百個實質脫離國家法治管轄的法外街區，充斥極端宗教勢力、黑幫與槍枝毒品，官方與學者卻長年對此視若無睹或美化掩飾，導致社會出現荒謬的反向同化現象。與此同時，右翼政客選前口號震天，選後卻為考量選票而向現實低頭。作者直言，若政治領袖不敢承擔政治代價去嚴懲青少年犯罪並強力執法、不願公開承認平行社會與整合失敗的事實，這張拖欠半世紀的政治帳單便永遠無法結清。

================================================

The elegant French are performing their rituals again this past weekend. And my ritual is to watch them perform their rituals. Watching those eager French students, fighting for their country and their future by smashing and looting in major cities, it’s hard not to be moved. Especially since they loot everything, except for pork, ham, and paper. This fact alone highlights. their innocent status and motives; it’s entirely about educational conditions, much like those rich peers who love to skip school yet support French students demanding better education. But I’m curious, France provides free healthcare, paid maternity leave, paid family leave, free daycare, and free pre-school education. Young women who don't want to have children get free contraceptives, and young men have free. condoms. Five weeks of paid vacation and a 35-hour work week. Grants and housing subsidies, and heavily subsidized higher education. Free libraries and museums, and free public transportation. Restaurants provide free water, and there are free job placement services. Whatever free things the leftists want, the French government has provided. Yet they are still protesting, still setting fires.

At the end of the day, these lazy, good-for-nothing leftists will never be satisfied, no matter how much free stuff you give them. Now they want free designer clothes and bags, free iPhones , and free daily necessities; if they can't get them for free, they loot— all in the name of education, they will never be satisfied. For many, France is completely finished. But I read something written by a French person on X. I think it’s very well written, so. I’m sharing it with everyone here. What happened in French cities over the past weekend didn't just fall from the sky, nor did it happen suddenly yesterday; it is the culmination of 50 years of French political decisions. It is the result accumulated by the left, the far-left, and the right taking turns in power. For decades, when facing crime, drug trafficking, violence, and threats to property and personal safety. We allowed a culture. of laxity to take root, choosing empty rhetoric, sociological excuses, and concessions on authority rather than firm and consistent law enforcement. The result is that some people have become accustomed to thinking they can smash, loot, and burn, without ever having to face real consequences. Education quality is declining, public services are crumbling, and the government can only watch helplessly as social integration fails completely,.

with the left and far-left denying or downplaying security and social cohesion issues for years. Once in power, the right often shouts loudly but does very little. Whether out of fear of unpopularity or electoral calculations, no one is truly willing to bear the political cost of restoring order and ending the concessions. Yes, the anger sparked by purchasing power and living conditions is real. The. looting, the vandalism, and the arson are not merely accidental products of a single weekend. They are the products of a system. A system that has year after year tolerated rules no longer applied equally to everyone. This is not the exclusive fault of one side, but a shared responsibility of everyone who has governed France since the 1970s . As long as we continue to choose posturing and denial rather than making difficult decisions, such weekends will. continue to happen. France is not finished; it is simply paying the bill for half a century of political cowardice. These are the faces of concession. This Frenchman’s perspective aligns with what I presented in the previous two episodes, when I said that all of Western Europe shares the same unpaid bill. There are three items on this bill: immigration, high welfare spending, and the massive loss of voter trust in centrist parties.

. Unless Western European governments pay these three debts, this scene will play out every weekend. In fact, it’s not just France; the tolerance and leniency of Western European governments toward crime have become a disgusting culture. The left and the far-left particularly love to whitewash criminals. They prefer to attribute crime to social structures, using lofty sociological terms to dilute individual. responsibility, or even cover it up and avoid talking about it. Just like the issue of grooming gangs in the UK, everyone knows that most of these people are unwilling to integrate into local European society. The government also knows that social integration policies have failed completely. But the left continues to pretend they don't know. And although the right knows, they are afraid to implement overly radical policies once in power. Many of the rioters in France today are the second generation of the 2005 riots. . The issue of integration has not been resolved at all in the past 20 years; instead, it has spread across Western and Northern Europe due to social media . The EU, which loves to talk about " supervision," what has it actually supervised? Or is it just supervising the right wing? As former French intelligence official Alain Chouet.

mentioned in his book "In the Hell of Islamist Separatism," there are 1,514 lawless neighborhoods in France that are effectively under the control of Sharia law. These lawless areas cover the greater Paris suburbs, such as Saint-Denis, the northern districts of Marseille, and the suburbs of Lyon, among others. These neighborhoods are rife with severe violence, gangs, drugs , firearms, and extremist religious ideologies, affecting four million. people. If you ask the government, they will give you bureaucratic excuses, claiming that France has no "no-go zones" that have truly detached from national sovereignty or where religious law replaces civil law. Those scholars sitting in their air-conditioned offices would also say these figures are exaggerated or distorted. Yeah. Then I invite them to walk into these lawless streets alone and see for themselves; didn't the past weekend serve as the best proof? In Paris,. Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Nice, and others, a massive number of shops were looted. In Limoges, a century-old town hall was burned down; those young people, supposedly demanding better educational conditions, showed no restraint in looting and burning. Some didn't even bother to cover their faces . When they lack even the most basic sense of shame, how can we talk about integration? The reality now is that the French are being "anti-integrated" by immigrants. Isn't this just the.

result of the leniency and tolerance shown by the left and far-left toward criminals over the past few decades? Is the right wing any better, then? Hard to say. Former President Sarkozy said as early as 2005 that he would use a pressure washer to clean up the housing projects, calling some of those young people "scum." That would certainly be politically incorrect today, but look at those young people rioting in Paris —if they aren't "scum," are they the. pillars of the nation? Sarkozy's words at the time were seen by the right wing as someone finally daring to tell the truth. Twenty years later, the underground economy in these working-class districts is more entrenched, drug trafficking is more open, violence against police and public institutions is normalized, and indicators of severe physical harm have risen sharply. Never mind Sarkozy from 20 years ago; even the current Italian Prime Minister Meloni, a right-winger,. faces similar issues. Riots are happening in Milan and Rome just the same. She got elected. She wanted to clear out illegal structures, but after two years, she still hasn't succeeded. We'll see if they manage to do it with another year. Even France's so-called far-right leader, Le Pen, was asked on TV whether some French Muslims might choose to leave France if she were.

elected. She clearly stated that would be wrong, because France is their country, they are French, and she and her party would not discriminate based on religious belief. Was her answer wrong? Of course it wasn't wrong; that is the most politically correct answer, 100 points. The problem is, do these so-called French people even consider France their country? You may not treat. citizens differently based on their religious beliefs, but these rioters treat you differently based on yours. For instance, in this recent riot, someone filmed how rioters skipped over shops owned by Muslims, while shops owned by those they consider "others" were looted clean. For example, this restaurant owned by a third-generation French Chinese immigrant was completely burned down. This is exactly what that Frenchman was talking about. Even if the right wing takes power, they shout loudly before the election but do very. little after. Why is that? For votes, of course. What other reason could there be? The immigration problem in Europe has long reached a point where no matter who leads, it cannot be solved. It's not that it's unsolvable, but that on both sides, no one is truly willing to bear the political cost required to restore order and stop the appeasement. How do you restore order and stop the appeasement? For example, increase penalties for juvenile offenders and cut back on those idiotic.

"universal love and tolerance" educational measures. Establish the toughest law enforcement units to march directly into lawless neighborhoods to enforce the law, showing them through action who the real boss of this country is, rather than waiting for things to explode and worsen, and openly admit that the integration policy for these immigrants has completely failed. Openly admit that parallel societies exist, and stop using moronic rhetoric like "social injustice" to whitewash criminals. Most. importantly, be willing to endure—or even ignore—the moral condemnation from "leftist" activists, the media, and idiotic international organizations , just like Israel stands its ground. Of all the measures to restore order and stop appeasement mentioned above, has any French government—whether left or right—ever dared to implement them? None. If Europe truly wants to restore order, they need someone willing to do the most unpopular things at the moment and endure the most. horrific backlash, just like Trump. Europe doesn't have a person like that either. France has even less. All France has is this face of appeasement. Most French people still choose to believe the same thing today: that they can maintain a luxurious lifestyle beyond their means by making others foot the bill, and then call it "social justice." Well, that's great. Then.

let's continue to witness these "social justice" events unfold in France every weekend. Know a little about everything , and life becomes a little more exciting. See you in the next episode.

沉默應對背後的品管死局與信任危機
